added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(s\in[1,2]\), \(M\ge2\), \(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\), and
\(u\in[-1,1]\), the construction satisfies
\[
 \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{fix}}\subset\mathcal P_n,
 \qquad c_{Q_u}=c_0,
 \qquad d_{Q_u}=\kappa_n,
 \qquad \theta_{Q_u}=u.
\]
Writing all divergences for the observed \(O_i\)-law, it also satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le
 2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s}
 n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le
 \left\{2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s}
 n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(a=(1-\kappa_n)/2\),
\(l=(1-\kappa_nu)/2\), and \(r=(1+\kappa_nu)/2\).
The type masses in \(\text{def:fixed-cutoff-bump-continuum}\) sum to one
and are nonnegative because \(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\).  Monotonicity follows
from \(D(0)=\mathbf 1\{R=A\}\) and
\(D(1)=\mathbf 1\{R\in\{A,C\}\}\).  Under assignment zero,
\[
 a r+\kappa_n\frac{1-u}{2}
 =\frac{1+\kappa_n}{2}l,
\]
whereas under assignment one,
\[
 a l+\kappa_n\frac{1+u}{2}
 =\frac{1+\kappa_n}{2}r.
\]
For assignment zero, the always-taker cell has outcome mean \(l\); the
first identity says that the combined never-taker--complier cell has the
same mean.  Thus \((D(0),Y(D(0)))\) has independent Bernoulli margins
\(((1-\kappa_n)/2,l)\).  The second identity gives independent margins
\(((1+\kappa_n)/2,r)\) for \((D(1),Y(D(1)))\).  Applying a common
type-independent binary kernel to the potential outcomes preserves this
independence for the actually assigned treatment.  Its denominators are
positive because every cutoff and target outcome mean is in
\([7/16,9/16]\).  This proves that the observable law is exactly the one
specified in the definition, without restricting the model class's
otherwise unrestricted treatment--outcome association.

The type masses do not depend on \(x\), so both potential-treatment
reduced forms are continuous at \(c_0\).  On either side, the Markov
kernel tends to the identity as \(x\to c_0\), since \(\psi(0)=1\).
Consequently, for each \(z\in\{0,1\}\), the reduced form
\(x\mapsto E_{Q_u}[Y(D(z))\mid X=x]\) tends from both sides to its value
under the common cutoff latent law.  This verifies the two causal
continuity assumptions.  The cutoff is interior, and the design is
uniform by construction.

It remains to check observable smoothness.  On \((-1,1)\),
\[
 \psi'(z)=-4z(1-z^2),
 \qquad
 \psi''(z)=-4+12z^2.
\]
Both \(\psi\) and \(\psi'\) vanish at \(z=\pm1\).  Pasting the
polynomial to zero therefore makes \(\psi\) globally continuously
differentiable.  Since \(|\psi''(z)|\le8\) away from the two support
boundaries, the continuous function \(\psi'\) is globally
\(8\)-Lipschitz.  Thus \(\psi\) is compactly supported and belongs to
\(C^{1,1}(\mathbb R)\), although \(\psi''\) may jump at the support
boundary.  Directly,
\(\|\psi\|_\infty\le1\), \(\|\psi'\|_\infty\le2\), and
\(\operatorname{Lip}(\psi')\le8\).  For every
\(\beta\in(0,1]\), the bounds
\[
 |\psi'(x)-\psi'(y)|
 \le 8|x-y|\quad\text{if }|x-y|\le1,
 \qquad
 |\psi'(x)-\psi'(y)|\le4\quad\text{if }|x-y|>1
\]
give \([\psi']_\beta\le8\).  Under the standard H\"older norms used in
\(\text{ass:observable-holder-extensions}\), these inequalities imply
\(H_s\le12\) for every \(s\in[1,2]\).

Let \(A=\kappa_n|u|/2\).  For \(u\ne0\), direct rescaling gives
\[
 \left\|A\psi\!\left(\frac{\cdot-c_0}{h_u}\right)
 \right\|_{\mathcal H^s}
 \le A H_s\max\{1,h_u^{-s}\}
 \le A H_s(1+h_u^{-s})
 \le \frac34+\frac{M}{8}.
\]
Indeed, for \(s=1\) the Lipschitz seminorm is multiplied by
\(Ah_u^{-1}\); for \(s=1+\beta\), \(0<\beta\le1\), the derivative
supremum is multiplied by \(Ah_u^{-1}\) and its \(\beta\)-H\"older
seminorm by \(Ah_u^{-1-\beta}=Ah_u^{-s}\).  If \(h_u\le1\), all
scaling factors are bounded by \(h_u^{-s}\), and if \(h_u>1\), they are
bounded by one.  Finally,
\(AH_sh_u^{-s}=M/8\) by the definition of \(h_u\), while
\(AH_s\le12/16=3/4\).  Adding the constant \(1/2\) gives a norm at most
\(5/4+M/8\le M\), using \(M\ge2\).  When \(u=0\), the outcome
extensions are constant and satisfy the same bound.  The treatment-side
extensions are constant and bounded by \(9/16\).  Thus all four
one-sided extensions belong to the declared radius-\(M\), order-\(s\)
balls.  Their jumps at \(c_0\) are \(\kappa_n\) and \(\kappa_nu\),
respectively.  Therefore the strength shell holds, and
\[
 d_{Q_u}=\kappa_n,
 \qquad y_{Q_u}=\kappa_nu,
 \qquad \theta_{Q_u}=y_{Q_u}/d_{Q_u}=u.
\]
The same value is obtained causally because the complier
potential-outcome means differ by \(u\).  This establishes membership in
\(\mathcal P_n\) and the asserted labels.

For the divergence calculation, \(Q_u\) and \(Q_0\) have the same
uniform \(X\)-law and the same conditional treatment law.  Conditional
independence in this witness therefore reduces their conditional joint
divergence to the outcome Bernoulli divergence.  If \(p=1/2+v\), then
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,1/2)
 \le \chi^2(\operatorname{Ber}(p),\operatorname{Ber}(1/2))
 =4v^2.
\]
The inequality follows from \(\log z\le z-1\), applied to the two
likelihood-ratio values and averaged under \(\operatorname{Ber}(p)\).
The absolute outcome-mean displacement is
\(A\psi((x-c_0)/h_u)\).  Since \(0\le\psi\le1\) and
\(\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(z)^2\,dz\le2\), uniform design yields, for
\(u\ne0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u,Q_0)
 &\le4A^2h_u\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(z)^2\,dz\\
 &\le2\kappa_n^2u^2h_u\\
 &=2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s}
   (\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(u=0\), both sides are zero.  Assumption
\(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\) makes the log likelihood ratio a sum of
\(n\) one-observation log likelihood ratios; taking expectation gives
exact Kullback--Leibler tensorization and proves the displayed
\(n\)-sample bound.

Finally, let \(p\) and \(q\) be any two densities and put
\(H^2(p,q)=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(\operatorname{TV}(p,q)\le H(p,q)\).  The pointwise inequality
\(-\log x\ge2(1-\sqrt x)\), integrated under \(p\) with \(x=q/p\),
gives \(H^2(p,q)\le\operatorname{KL}(p,q)\), with the extended-real
convention when absolute continuity fails.  Hence
\(\operatorname{TV}(p,q)\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(p,q)}\).  Applying
this derived inequality to the product-law Kullback--Leibler bound proves
the asserted total-variation inequality.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(a=1-\alpha\).  If \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), then
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge G_\alpha(\tau_n)
 =\begin{cases}
 2a-\dfrac{16}{3}\sqrt{\tau_n},
   &0\le\tau_n\le a^2/16,\\[6pt]
 \dfrac{a^3}{24\tau_n},&\tau_n>a^2/16.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover, there are constants \(c_{\mathrm{fix}}>0\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{low}}>0\), depending only on \(s\), \(M\), and
\(\alpha\), such that for every \(n\ge1\) and
\(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{fix}}\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\},
 \qquad
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix any interval rule \(I_n\) satisfying the honesty constraint in
\(\text{def:minimax-length}\), and first suppose \(\kappa_n\le1/16\).
By \(\text{prop:moving-cutoff-membership-kl}\), every \(P_t\) belongs to
\(\mathcal P_n\), has effect label \(t\), and satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \le4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
\]
Honesty under \(P_t\) and the defining variational inequality for total
variation therefore imply, for every \(t\in[-1,1]\),
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
 \ge P_t^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
     -\operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \ge1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
\]
The left side is nonnegative.  To justify the coverage integration
directly, fix \(m\ge1\) and use the equally spaced grid
\(t_j=-1+2j/m\), \(j=0,\ldots,m\).  For every connected
\(I_n\subset[-1,1]\), the number of grid points in \(I_n\) is at most
\(1+m|I_n|/2\).  Hence, deterministically,
\[
 |I_n|\ge\frac2m\sum_{j=0}^m\mathbf 1\{t_j\in I_n\}-\frac2m.
\]
Taking expectations uses only linearity for this finite sum.  Applying
the preceding probability bound and then letting \(m\to\infty\), the
Riemann sums converge because
\(t\mapsto[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}]_+\) is continuous.  Therefore
\[
 E_{P_0}|I_n|
 \ge2\int_0^1[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_nt}]_+\,dt
 =G_\alpha(\tau_n).
\]
Because \(P_0\in\mathcal P_n\), the worst-case expected length of every
honest rule is at least this quantity; taking the infimum over such rules
proves the first inequality.

To evaluate the integral, write \(a=1-\alpha\).  If
\(\tau_n\le a^2/16\), its integrand is nonnegative throughout
\([0,1]\), and
\[
 2\int_0^1(a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt})\,dt
 =2a-\frac{16}{3}\sqrt{\tau_n}.
\]
If \(\tau_n>a^2/16\), the positive region ends at
\(t_0=a^2/(16\tau_n)\), and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 2\int_0^{t_0}(a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt})\,dt
 &=2\left(at_0-\frac83\sqrt{\tau_n}t_0^{3/2}\right)\\
 &=\frac{a^3}{24\tau_n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the closed form in
\(\text{def:integrated-slope-lower-function}\).

We next use the fixed-cutoff family.  Let
\[
 p_s=2+\frac1s,
 \qquad
 C_b=2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s},
 \qquad
 \gamma=\min\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{(1-2\alpha)^2}{16C_b}\right)^{1/p_s}\right\},
\]
and choose the positive label
\[
 u_n=\gamma\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Since \(\rho_n=n^{-s/(2s+1)}\), one has
\(n\rho_n^{p_s}=1\).  If \(\rho_n\le\kappa_n\), then
\(n(\kappa_nu_n)^{p_s}=\gamma^{p_s}\); if
\(\rho_n>\kappa_n\), the left side is at most
\(\gamma^{p_s}n\rho_n^{p_s}=\gamma^{p_s}\).  By
\(\text{prop:fixed-cutoff-bump-membership-kl}\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le\sqrt{C_b\gamma^{p_s}}
 \le\frac{1-2\alpha}{4}.
\]
Both laws are in \(\mathcal P_n\).  Honesty and total variation imply
under \(Q_0\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{0,u_n\in I_n\}
 &\ge1-Q_0^{\otimes n}\{0\notin I_n\}
       -Q_0^{\otimes n}\{u_n\notin I_n\}\\
 &\ge1-2\alpha-
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})\\
 &\ge\frac34(1-2\alpha).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On this event, connectedness of \(I_n\subset[-1,1]\) forces
\(|I_n|\ge u_n\).  Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n|
 \ge E_{Q_0}|I_n|
 \ge \frac34(1-2\alpha)\gamma
       \min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Taking the infimum proves the fixed-cutoff inequality with
\(c_{\mathrm{fix}}=3(1-2\alpha)\gamma/4>0\).

It remains to combine the two lower bounds.  The displayed formula for
\(G_\alpha\) implies, for every \(\tau>0\),
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau)
 \ge \frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}\min\{1,\tau^{-1}\}.
\]
Indeed, below the breakpoint its minimum is
\(2(1-\alpha)/3\), between the breakpoint and one the second branch is
at least \((1-\alpha)^3/24\), and above one the second branch equals
\((1-\alpha)^3/(24\tau)\).  Put
\[
 A_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n},
 \qquad B_n=\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}.
\]
When \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), the two lower bounds imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 &\ge \max\left\{
 c_{\mathrm{fix}}\min(1,A_n),
 \frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}\min(1,B_n)\right\}\\
 &\ge \frac12\min\left\{c_{\mathrm{fix}},
 \frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}\right\}
 \{\min(1,A_n)+\min(1,B_n)\}\\
 &\ge \frac12\min\left\{c_{\mathrm{fix}},
 \frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}\right\}
 \min(1,A_n+B_n)\\
 &=\frac12\min\left\{c_{\mathrm{fix}},
 \frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}\right\}r_n.
 \end{aligned}
\]

Finally suppose \(1/16<\kappa_n\le1/8\).  The location term is then
absorbed by the fixed-cutoff term, because
\[
 \frac{B_n}{A_n}
 =\frac1{n\kappa_n^2\rho_n}
 \le256\,n^{-(s+1)/(2s+1)}
 \le256.
\]
Here we used \(n\rho_n=n^{(s+1)/(2s+1)}\ge1\).  Consequently,
\[
 r_n=\min(1,A_n+B_n)
 \le257\min(1,A_n),
\]
and the fixed-cutoff inequality gives
\(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge(c_{\mathrm{fix}}/257)r_n\).
Taking \(C_{\mathrm{low}}\) to be the minimum of the positive constants
obtained in the two cases completes the proof.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{prof}}\), construct \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\)
and prove
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
 P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
for every strength sequence.  On each critical component of
\(\mathfrak R\) whose value is evaluated by \(\mathcal V_\alpha\), prove
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|
 -L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), prove
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}|
 \asymp L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n.
\]
The upper comparison must keep the local stochastic contribution
\(\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) separate from the remainders
\(\zeta_n\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont},n}\),
\(|\mathcal G_c|\exp[-C_{\mathrm{sep}}n\kappa_n^2h_n/4]\),
\(2\delta_n\), and twice the maximal probability of each fallback branch
in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\); the last four expected-length
remainders must be \(o(r_n)\), and \(\zeta_n=o(1)\).  No upper rate or
critical constant is claimed from \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\), from
population separation, or from marginal profiling alone.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The recovered-regime lower-comparison request is no longer open: \(\text{thm:integrated-and-bump-lower-frontier}\) proves the stronger all-strength inequality under the unchanged model class. Removing that already-settled clause relocates the lower frontier to a proved theorem while preserving every unresolved honesty, upper-risk, fallback, and attainment obligation.

proposed.name: \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{fix}}
proposed.construction:
Let
\[
 \psi(z)=(1-z^2)^2\mathbf 1\{|z|\le1\},
 \qquad H_s=\|\psi\|_{\mathcal H^s(\mathbb R)},
\]
where the norm is the same standard H\"older norm used for the
radius-\(M\) balls in \(\text{ass:observable-holder-extensions}\).
The function \(\psi\) is compactly supported and belongs to
\(C^{1,1}(\mathbb R)\): both \(\psi\) and \(\psi'\) vanish at the
support boundary, whereas \(\psi''\) may jump there.  Put \(h_0=0\);
for \(u\ne0\), put
\[
 h_u=\left(\frac{4H_s\kappa_n|u|}{M}\right)^{1/s}.
\]
Under \(Q_u\), the observations are independent and identically
distributed, \(X\) is uniform on \([0,1]\), and the cutoff is
\(c_0=1/2\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), the observed variables \(D\) and
\(Y\) are independent Bernoulli variables.  The treatment mean is
\((1-\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x<c_0\) and \((1+\kappa_n)/2\) for
\(x\ge c_0\).  For \(u\ne0\), the outcome mean is
\[
 \frac12-\frac{\kappa_nu}{2}
 \psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right)\quad(x<c_0),
 \qquad
 \frac12+\frac{\kappa_nu}{2}
 \psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right)\quad(x\ge c_0).
\]
For \(u=0\), the outcome mean is \(1/2\) on both sides.

The full-data lift is defined as follows.  At the cutoff, assign type
masses \((1-\kappa_n)/2\), \(\kappa_n\), and
\((1-\kappa_n)/2\) to \(A\), \(C\), and \(N\), respectively.
Always-takers have a common binary potential outcome of mean
\((1-\kappa_nu)/2\), never-takers have a common binary potential outcome
of mean \((1+\kappa_nu)/2\), and complier potential outcomes have means
\((1-u)/2\) and \((1+u)/2\) under treatment zero and one, respectively.
Take the two complier potential outcomes conditionally independent, and
keep these response-type masses fixed for every \(x\).  Away from the
cutoff, start from this common cutoff law.  On the observed
side \(z\), apply to both binary potential outcomes the same
type-independent binary Markov kernel that maps the relevant cutoff-side
outcome mean \(b\) to the displayed target mean \(g\): when \(g\ge b\),
retain every one and change a zero to one with probability
\((g-b)/(1-b)\); when \(g<b\), retain every zero and retain a one with
probability \(g/b\).  Use conditionally independent auxiliary coins.
Let
\[
 \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{fix}}=\{Q_u:u\in[-1,1]\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This explicit causal lift and observable bump family is the same-class witness requested for the fixed-cutoff minimax lower term.
The retained label-dependent coverage integral has the directive's explicit piecewise closed form.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\vartheta\in\Theta:\inf_{c\in\mathcal G_c}\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\}\). The proved minimax converse is \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) over the full declared strength shell; the matching profile upper comparison \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n\) remains proposed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: After relocating the proved all-strength lower comparison, uniform continuum honesty and minimax expected-length attainment for \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\), including the separately displayed upper-rate remainders and fallback probabilities, remain open.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact-grid method-of-types calibration and population profile separation do not transfer a continuously indexed true cutoff and effect to the candidate-specific grids and inner--outer sieves. The frozen core still lacks uniform control of the moved-discontinuity strip, localized stochastic profile width, certificate and solver fallbacks, and the critical-face decision value; the unresolved critical experiment also prevents equality with \(L_n^\star\) on finite-positive faces.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact-grid feasible-truth event was combined with the established deterministic false-split gap, and the lower-risk part was attacked separately by the moving-cutoff coverage integral and the fixed-cutoff bump continuum. This closes the entire minimax lower frontier but supplies no uniform continuum-transfer or profile upper-risk theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The all-strength minimax lower comparison is now closed separately:
\(\text{thm:integrated-and-bump-lower-frontier}\) proves
\(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n\) for the entire declared
strength shell.  Its moving-cutoff component gives the stronger explicit
bound \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), and its fixed-cutoff
bump component gives
\(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge c_{\mathrm{fix}}
\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\).  Independently, the established exact-grid
calibration proposition accepts a grid-aligned true pair with conditional
probability at least
\(1-\delta_n/(|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|)\), and returning
\(\Theta\) on every listed fallback preserves that coverage.  The
established population separation theorem supplies the deterministic gap
\(C_{\mathrm{sep}}\kappa_n^2\min\{|c-c_P|,h_n\}\).  These are the complete
lower, exact-grid calibration, and population-localization layers; they
do not prove continuum honesty or the profile interval's upper risk.

prose_updates.tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. The moving-cutoff continuum now gives the explicit finite-sample lower value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), and a causal-valid fixed-cutoff bump continuum gives the nonparametric term \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\). Together they prove the all-strength converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) under the unchanged binary H{\"o}lder-margin class, while the existing upper bound gives the exact flat-face limit \(2(1-\alpha)\). Finite-grid four-cell calibration remains valid for every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells. The open kernel is the \(s=1\) critical decision value and a continuum-honest, support-wide profile interval with controlled stochastic, discretization, certificate, and fallback remainders; no profile upper rate or finite-positive critical value is claimed as proved.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy inference, sharp-RD unknown-cutoff rates, generic weak-identification decision theory, and Bayesian propagation of cutoff uncertainty have been developed separately. None supplies an all-strength minimax converse together with an attaining honest connected interval when the cutoff and fuzzy denominator weaken jointly; the converse is now proved here, whereas attainment remains open.
project_justification.niche: The preserved binary uniform-design class makes two complementary causal lifts explicit while leaving the observable treatment--outcome association unrestricted. A moving-cutoff continuum measures slope-location ambiguity and a fixed-cutoff compact bump measures ordinary nonparametric jump difficulty, producing a nonregular location/effect problem that is neither a fixed-boundary modulus problem nor a parametric unknown-break problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the lower frontier by combining the integrated moving-cutoff value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\) with a same-class fixed-cutoff bump bound, yielding \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) for every declared strength. It also defines a support-wide four-cell profile and coarsened exact calibration that leave association free. The matching upper frontier, the complete critical experiment, and a total attaining interval remain the stated unresolved contribution.

prose_updates.related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1) give weak-identification-robust inference at a fixed known cutoff; they do not address translated cutoff/effect ambiguity. The fixed-cutoff bump continuum recovers the usual nonparametric weak-denominator difficulty inside the present binary class, while the moving-cutoff continuum adds the distinct \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) difficulty and its explicit integrated value \(G_\alpha\). Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) study unknown-location behavior predominantly in sharp designs, without this weak causal ratio or connected honest-length criterion. Elliott and M{\"u}ller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) motivate process experiments for moderate unknown breaks, but do not solve the present H{\"o}lder-margin decision problem. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis; Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes. None of these results proves the still-open support-wide profile upper bound over the translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) motivate retaining the full joint outcome--treatment law. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model has no outcome-variance, null-residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor, and the new lower bound adds none. The proved results now include the moving-cutoff causal lift and its Kullback--Leibler bound, the explicit integrated lower value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), the exact flat-face limit, the fixed-cutoff compact-bump causal lift and its \(n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\) divergence bound, and the all-strength minimax converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). Exact finite-grid four-cell calibration and population false-split separation are also proved, uniformly over permitted binary treatment--outcome associations. These facts do not establish continuum honesty, an upper expected-length rate, or attainment by \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\). The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, localized stochastic profile bound, and negligible fallback risk remain open. A matching upper comparison is still only a proposed goal on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence for the full class, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.

statement_notes.justification: The two legal causal continua isolate the location-slope and fixed-cutoff nonparametric sources of difficulty and combine to prove the complete lower half of the candidate all-strength frontier.
statement_notes.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy procedures do not supply the moving-location term, while sharp unknown-cutoff rates do not supply the weak causal-ratio term; the theorem derives both within one unchanged full model.
statement_notes.consumer: An analyst obtains a design-independent impossibility benchmark: no honest connected interval can beat \(r_n\), even before the proposed profile procedure is shown to attain it.

statement_notes.justification: With the minimax lower frontier settled separately, the remaining task is a single total interval that converts finite-grid calibration into continuum-uniform honesty and a matching upper expected-length guarantee.
statement_notes.gap: Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) condition out a functional nuisance in Gaussian-process moment models, while Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024) invert weak-identification-robust tests at a known cutoff. None supplies the required certified four-cell continuum transfer, fallback control, or critical-face attainment under an unknown cutoff.
statement_notes.consumer: The interval would give a frequentist benchmark for unknown or administratively uncertain eligibility thresholds, including the binary HIV-retention application studied by Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(a=1-\alpha\).  The first conclusion of \(\text{thm:integrated-and-bump-lower-frontier}\) and \(\text{def:integrated-slope-lower-function}\) give
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge G_\alpha(\tau_n)
 =2\int_0^1[a-4\sqrt{\tau_n t}]_+\,dt.
\]
For \(0\le t\le1\), one has \(\sqrt{\tau_n t}\le\sqrt{\tau_n}\); monotonicity of the positive-part map therefore gives
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau_n)
 \ge 2\int_0^1[a-4\sqrt{\tau_n}]_+\,dt
 =2[a-4\sqrt{\tau_n}]_+.
\]
This proves the asserted lower bound.

For the upper bound, define the following measurable rule from the observed sample:
\[
 I_n^0(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
 =
 \begin{cases}
   \Theta,&X_1\le1-\alpha,\\
   \{0\},&X_1>1-\alpha.
 \end{cases}
\]
Both possible values are connected subsets of \(\Theta\).  By ass:uniform-running-variable, every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) satisfies
\[
 P\{\theta_P\in I_n^0\}\ge P\{X_1\le1-\alpha\}=1-\alpha
\]
and
\[
 E_P|I_n^0|=2P\{X_1\le1-\alpha\}=2(1-\alpha).
\]
Thus \(I_n^0\) is an admissible witness in \(\text{def:minimax-length}\), which proves \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\le2(1-\alpha)\).

If \(\tau_n\to0\), then the displayed lower bound tends to \(2a\), while the upper bound is identically \(2a\).  The squeeze theorem gives
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\longrightarrow2(1-\alpha).
\]
Finally, fix \(s>1\) and suppose that \(\lambda_n\) remains in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\).  If \(\kappa_n\not\to0\), then along a subsequence \(\kappa_n\ge\epsilon>0\).  On that subsequence the definition of \(\lambda_n\) implies
\[
 \lambda_n
 =\frac{n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}}{\log(e/\kappa_n)}
 \ge \frac{n\epsilon^{2+1/s}}{\log(e/\epsilon)},
\]
where we used \(\kappa_n\le1/8\) to note that \(x\mapsto\log(e/x)\) is decreasing and hence \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\le\log(e/\epsilon)\).  The right-hand side diverges, contradicting boundedness of \(\lambda_n\).  Hence \(\kappa_n\to0\).  Rearranging the defining identity for \(\lambda_n\) gives
\[
 \tau_n
 =\lambda_n\kappa_n^{1-1/s}\log(e/\kappa_n).
\]
Because \(1-1/s>0\), the elementary limit \(x^{1-1/s}\log(e/x)\to0\) as \(x\downarrow0\), together with boundedness of \(\lambda_n\), yields \(\tau_n\to0\).  The preceding squeeze then proves the final assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\kappa_n\in(0,1/8]\), the fixed-cutoff family satisfies \(\mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{bump}}\subset\mathcal P_n\), \(d_{Q_u}=\kappa_n\), and \(\theta_{Q_u}=u\) for every \(u\in[-1,1]\).  Moreover, for every such \(u\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le 2\left(\frac{32}{M}\right)^{1/s}
 n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s},
\]
and
\[
 \chi^2(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le
 \exp\!\left\{2\left(\frac{32}{M}\right)^{1/s}
 n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\right\}-1.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\kappa=\kappa_n\).  The cutoff is \(c_0=1/2\), so ass:interior-cutoff holds.  The construction gives the uniform law for \(X\), and independent replication gives ass:iid-sampling.  The response-type probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one because \(0<\kappa\le1/8\); they give
\[
 E_{Q_u}[D(0)\mid X=c_0]=\frac{1-\kappa}{2},
 \quad
 E_{Q_u}[D(1)\mid X=c_0]=\frac{1+\kappa}{2}.
\]
They are kept fixed with \(x\), so both potential-treatment reduced forms are continuous at \(c_0\), establishing ass:potential-treatment-continuity.  Their difference is \(\kappa\), whence
\[
 d_{Q_u}=\kappa,
\]
which satisfies ass:local-compliance-strength.

We next verify the outcome part of the lift.  Put
\[
 a=\frac{1-\kappa}{2},\quad
 l=\frac{1-u\kappa}{2},\quad
 r=\frac{1+u\kappa}{2}.
\]
Under assignment zero, the treated units are precisely the always-takers and have outcome mean \(l\).  The untreated units are never-takers and compliers, and the identity
\[
 ar+\kappa\frac{1-u}{2}
 =\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\,l
\]
shows that their outcome mean is also \(l\).  Thus \(D\) and \(Y\) are independent at the cutoff under assignment zero, with outcome mean \(l\).  Similarly,
\[
 al+\kappa\frac{1+u}{2}
 =\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\,r,
\]
so under assignment one the conditional outcome mean is \(r\) for both treatment values.  This proves the claimed independent observed law at \(c_0\).  On either side, the type-independent binary channel in \(\text{def:fixed-cutoff-bump-continuum}\) maps the appropriate cutoff mean to the displayed outcome mean and preserves its independence from \(D\).  Since \(\psi(0)=1\), the channel's flip probability tends to zero as \(x\to c_0\) from the relevant side.  Hence each map \(x\mapsto E_{Q_u}[Y(D(z))\mid X=x]\) is continuous at \(c_0\), which is ass:potential-outcome-continuity.  The channel denominators are positive because \(l,r\in[7/16,9/16]\).  Monotonicity, exclusion, and consistency hold by the displayed potential-variable construction.

It remains to verify the observable H\"older restriction.  On \((-1,1)\),
\[
 \psi'(z)=-4z(1-z^2),\quad \psi''(z)=-4+12z^2.
\]
Both \(\psi\) and \(\psi'\) match their zero exterior values at \(\{-1,1\}\), while \(|\psi'|\le2\) and the globally defined \(\psi'\) is Lipschitz with constant at most \(8\).  For every \(\beta\in(0,1]\), splitting according as \(|z-z'|\le1\) or \(|z-z'|>1\) gives
\[
 [\psi']_{\beta}
 :=\sup_{z\ne z'}\frac{|\psi'(z)-\psi'(z')|}{|z-z'|^\beta}
 \le8.
\]
For \(u\ne0\), set \(A=\kappa|u|/2\) and \(h=h_u\).  The scaled bump has supremum at most \(A\).  When \(s=1\), its Lipschitz seminorm is at most
\[
 \frac{2A}{h}=\frac{\kappa|u|}{h}=\frac{M}{32}.
\]
When \(1<s\le2\), putting \(\beta=s-1\) gives
\[
 \left\|\frac{d}{dx}\left[A\psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h}\right)\right]\right\|_\infty
 \le\frac{2A}{h}
 =\frac{M}{32}h^{s-1}
 \le\frac{M}{16}
\]
because \(h^s=32\kappa|u|/M\le2\), and
\[
 \left[\frac{d}{dx}\left\{A\psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h}\right)\right\}\right]_{s-1}
 \le\frac{8A}{h^s}=\frac{M}{8}.
\]
The outcome extensions take values in \([7/16,9/16]\).  Since \(M\ge2\), the preceding supremum, derivative, and H\"older-seminorm bounds, including their sum under the usual norm convention, are strictly below radius \(M\).  The treatment extensions are constant.  Thus ass:observable-holder-extensions holds; for \(u=0\) it is immediate.  We have proved \(Q_u\in\mathcal P_n\).

The reduced-form outcome jump is
\[
 y_{Q_u}=r-l=\kappa u.
\]
Since \(d_{Q_u}=\kappa>0\), the definition of \(\theta_P\) yields \(\theta_{Q_u}=u\).
The causal label agrees with this observed-law functional rather than being imposed by notation: the specified complier potential-outcome margins give
\[
 E_{Q_u}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_0]
 =\frac{1+u}{2}-\frac{1-u}{2}=u.
\]

Finally, compare the observed one-unit laws under \(Q_u\) and \(Q_0\).  When \(u=0\), both claimed divergence bounds are immediate because the two laws coincide.  Hence suppose \(u\ne0\).  Their running-variable laws and conditional treatment laws agree.  Conditional on \(X=x\), their outcome means differ by
\[
 \delta_u(x)
 =\frac{\kappa u}{2}\psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right)
\]
up to a sign that is immaterial below.  For a Bernoulli law of mean \(1/2+\delta\), the inequality \(\log v\le v-1\), applied cellwise, gives
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(1/2+\delta,1/2)
 \le \chi^2(\operatorname{Bern}(1/2+\delta),\operatorname{Bern}(1/2))
 =4\delta^2.
\]
Consequently, using the uniform design and then changing variables,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u,Q_0)
 &\le \kappa^2u^2\int_0^1
 \psi^2\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right)\,dx\\
 &\le \kappa^2u^2h_u\int_{-1}^1\psi^2(z)\,dz\\
 &\le2\left(\frac{32}{M}\right)^{1/s}(\kappa|u|)^{2+1/s},
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(0\le\psi\le1\) was used in the last line.  The identical calculation gives the same upper bound for \(\chi^2(Q_u,Q_0)\).  Independence implies KL tensorization, proving the first displayed bound.  If \(L=dQ_u/dQ_0\), independence also gives
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^nL(O_i)^2\right]
 =\{1+\chi^2(Q_u,Q_0)\}^n.
\]
Using \((1+x)^n\le e^{nx}\) proves the asserted product chi-square bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n\) with \(\kappa_n\le1/16\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge G_\alpha(\tau_n)
 \ge\frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{1}{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}.
\]
For each fixed \(s\in[1,2]\), \(M\ge2\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\), there is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{bump}}(s,M,\alpha)>0\) such that, for every \(n\) and every \(\kappa_n\in(0,1/8]\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{bump}}(s,M,\alpha)
 \min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Consequently, there are constants \(C(s,M,\alpha)>0\) and \(N(s)\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n\ge N(s)\) and all \(\kappa_n\in(0,1/8]\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C(s,M,\alpha)r_n.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(a=1-\alpha\), and let \(I_n\) be any interval rule satisfying the honesty constraint in \(\text{def:minimax-length}\).  For \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), prop:moving-cutoff-membership-kl gives, for every \(t\in[-1,1]\),
\[
 P_t\in\mathcal P_n,\quad \theta_{P_t}=t,
 \quad
 \operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \le4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
\]
Honesty and the defining supremum property of total variation imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_0^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
 &\ge P_t^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
   -\operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})\\
 &\ge a-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The left-hand side is nonnegative, so it is at least \([a-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}]_+\).  Pathwise, the definition of Lebesgue length gives
\[
 |I_n|=\int_{-1}^1\mathbf 1\{t\in I_n\}\,dt.
\]
Integrating first for nonnegative simple functions and then increasing to the displayed indicator identity yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{P_0}|I_n|
 &=\int_{-1}^1P_0^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}\,dt\\
 &\ge2\int_0^1[a-4\sqrt{\tau_n t}]_+\,dt
 =G_\alpha(\tau_n).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Because \(P_0\in\mathcal P_n\), taking first the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and then the infimum over honest \(I_n\) proves the first inequality.

To evaluate the integral, if \(0\le\tau\le a^2/16\), the integrand is positive throughout \([0,1]\), and
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau)
 =2\left(a-4\sqrt\tau\int_0^1t^{1/2}\,dt\right)
 =2a-\frac{16}{3}\sqrt\tau.
\]
If \(\tau>a^2/16\), the positive region ends at \(t_0=a^2/(16\tau)\), so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_\alpha(\tau)
 &=2\left(at_0-4\sqrt\tau\int_0^{t_0}t^{1/2}\,dt\right)\\
 &=2\left(\frac{a^3}{16\tau}-\frac{a^3}{24\tau}\right)
 =\frac{a^3}{24\tau}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This verifies \(\text{def:integrated-slope-lower-function}\), including equality at the elbow.  On the first branch, \(G_\alpha(\tau)\ge2a/3\); on the second branch, splitting further according as \(\tau<1\) or \(\tau\ge1\) gives
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau)\ge\frac{a^3}{24}\min\{1,1/\tau\}.
\]
Since \(a^3/24\le2a/3\), the same inequality holds on both branches and also at \(\tau=0\).  Substitution of \(\tau_n=n\kappa_n^3\) proves the second slope inequality.

We now use the fixed-cutoff continuum.  Set
\[
 p=2+\frac1s,\quad
 B=2\left(\frac{32}{M}\right)^{1/s},\quad
 \gamma=\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\},
\]
and choose
\[
 b=\min\{1,(\gamma/B)^{1/p}\},
 \quad
 u_n=b\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Then \(0<u_n\le1\), \(\kappa_nu_n\le b\rho_n\), and the definitions of \(p\) and \(\rho_n\) give
\[
 n\rho_n^p
 =n\left(n^{-s/(2s+1)}\right)^{(2s+1)/s}=1.
\]
By prop:fixed-cutoff-bump-membership-kl,
\[
 \chi^2(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le e^{Bb^p}-1\le e^\gamma-1=(1-2\alpha)^2.
\]
For completeness, if \(L_n=dQ_{u_n}^{\otimes n}/dQ_0^{\otimes n}\), then Cauchy--Schwarz gives directly
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|L_n-1|
 \le\frac12\{E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}(L_n-1)^2\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}.
\]
Honesty at \(Q_0\) and \(Q_{u_n}\), followed by this comparison, yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{0,u_n\in I_n\}
 &\ge Q_0^{\otimes n}\{0\in I_n\}
   +Q_0^{\otimes n}\{u_n\in I_n\}-1\\
 &\ge (1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha)
   -\operatorname{TV}(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})-1\\
 &\ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
On this event, connectedness of \(I_n\subset[-1,1]\) and \(u_n>0\) imply \([0,u_n]\subset I_n\), hence \(|I_n|\ge u_n\).  Therefore
\[
 E_{Q_0}|I_n|
 \ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}u_n
 =\frac{(1-2\alpha)b}{2}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Membership of \(Q_0\) in \(\mathcal P_n\), followed by the same supremum and infimum operations as above, proves the bump lower bound with
\[
 c_{\mathrm{bump}}(s,M,\alpha)=\frac{(1-2\alpha)b}{2}>0.
\]

It remains to combine the two bounds.  Put
\[
 x_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n},\quad
 y_n=\frac{1}{n\kappa_n^3}.
\]
For nonnegative \(x,y\),
\[
 \min\{1,x+y\}
 \le\min\{1,x\}+\min\{1,y\}
 \le2\max\{\min(1,x),\min(1,y)\}.
\]
Thus, when \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), the bump and integrated-slope bounds imply
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge\frac12\min\left\{c_{\mathrm{bump}}(s,M,\alpha),\frac{a^3}{24}\right\}
 \min\{1,x_n+y_n\}.
\]
For \(\kappa_n>1/16\), direct calculation gives
\[
 \frac{y_n}{x_n}
 =n^{-(s+1)/(2s+1)}\kappa_n^{-2}
 <256n^{-(s+1)/(2s+1)}.
\]
Choose \(N(s)\) so that the last expression is at most one for \(n\ge N(s)\).  Then \(y_n\le x_n\), and hence
\[
 r_n=\min\{1,x_n+y_n\}
 \le2\min\{1,x_n\}.
\]
The bump lower bound consequently gives \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge(c_{\mathrm{bump}}/2)r_n\) on this remaining strength range.  Taking the smaller of the two positive constants completes the all-strength conclusion.  This last comparison also makes explicit why, when \(\kappa_n>1/16\), the term \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) is asymptotically absorbed by the fixed-cutoff term under the unchanged model class.

proposed.name: \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{bump}}
proposed.construction:
Let
\[
 \psi(z)=(1-z^2)^2\mathbf 1\{|z|\le1\}.
\]
This function is compactly supported and belongs to \(C^{1,1}(\mathbb R)\): both \(\psi\) and \(\psi'\) vanish at \(z=\pm1\), whereas \(\psi''\) has a jump there.  Fix \(c_0=1/2\).  For \(u\in[-1,1]\setminus\{0\}\), put
\[
 h_u=\left(\frac{32\kappa_n|u|}{M}\right)^{1/s}.
\]
Under \(Q_u\), let \(X\) be uniform on \([0,1]\), set \(c_{Q_u}=c_0\) and \(Z=\mathbf 1\{X\ge c_0\}\), and impose \(D=D(Z)\) and \(Y=Y(D)\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), let the resulting \(D\) and \(Y\) be independent Bernoulli variables.  The conditional treatment mean is \((1-\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x<c_0\) and \((1+\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x\ge c_0\).  The conditional outcome mean is
\[
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle \frac12-\frac{\kappa_nu}{2}
 \psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right),&x<c_0,\\[6pt]
 \displaystyle \frac12+\frac{\kappa_nu}{2}
 \psi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right),&x\ge c_0.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(u=0\), define \(Q_0\) by the same treatment law and by an independent Bernoulli outcome of mean \(1/2\).

The full-data lift is fixed as follows.  At \(x=c_0\), assign response-type probabilities
\[
 Q_u(R=A)=Q_u(R=N)=\frac{1-\kappa_n}{2},
 \quad Q_u(R=C)=\kappa_n.
\]
For always-takers let \(Y(0)=Y(1)\) have mean \((1-u\kappa_n)/2\), and for never-takers let \(Y(0)=Y(1)\) have mean \((1+u\kappa_n)/2\).  For compliers choose a binary coupling whose two marginal means are
\[
 E_{Q_u}[Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_0]=\frac{1-u}{2},
 \quad
 E_{Q_u}[Y(1)\mid R=C,X=c_0]=\frac{1+u}{2}.
\]
Use \(D(0)=\mathbf 1\{R=A\}\) and \(D(1)=\mathbf 1\{R\in\{A,C\}\}\).  Away from \(c_0\), keep the response-type probabilities fixed.  On side \(z\in\{0,1\}\), apply to each potential outcome, independently of response type, the same binary Markov kernel taking its side-specific cutoff mean \(b\) to the displayed side-specific outcome mean \(m\): if \(m\ge b\), flip a zero to one with probability \((m-b)/(1-b)\), and if \(m<b\), flip a one to zero with probability \((b-m)/b\).  The continuum named by this construction is
\[
 \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{bump}}=\{Q_u:u\in[-1,1]\}.
\]

proposed.statement:
For \(\kappa_n\le1/16\),
\[
 2[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n}]_+
 \le L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \le 2(1-\alpha).
\]
Hence \(\tau_n\to0\) implies \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\to2(1-\alpha)\). If \(s>1\) is fixed and \(\lambda_n\) remains in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), then the same limit holds.
proposed.justification: This identifies an exact nonshrinking phase and removes a spurious higher-smoothness transition based only on location entropy.
proposed.gap: Mikusheva (2010) links weak-instrument test power to confidence-set length, while the banked parent obtained only a two-label location mixture; neither yields the full-label coefficient \(2(1-\alpha)\) in this unknown-cutoff class.
proposed.consumer: An analyst can recognize regimes in which any apparently narrow interval must owe its informativeness to restrictions stronger than the maintained H\"older class.
